name: Tolai-Nakanai-Trade
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct PNG trade pidgin; Glottolog lists no references; no description of any kind located

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record tola1236 and reference record 114872 (Hammarström et al.)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog's sole reference (MED type 'wordlist_or_less', 7 pp.) is Dutton & Ross 1992; the languoid is classified under the pseudo-family 'Minigir-based pidgin' (mini1258). The WORLD_TARGETS record said 'Glottolog lists no references', which is not quite right: the JSON carries this one MED reference.

sources.citation: Dutton, Tom & Malcolm Ross. 1992. A note on Hees' 'Tolai-Nakanai' trade language. Language and Linguistics in Melanesia 23(2): 198-204.
sources.note: Squib re-analysing Hees' five sentences with interlinear glosses; concludes (pp. 202-203) the trade language 'was basically Minigir with some Meramera/Nakanai pronouns and a small measure of simplification' and 'hardly a pidgin as this term is usually understood'. Phonological remarks (pp. 202-203) cover only n>l, r>l and loss of u- in ura; nothing on stress or accent.

sources.citation: Hees, Friedrich. 1915-16. Ein Beitrag aus den Sagen und Erzählungen der Nakanai (Neupommern, Südsee). Anthropos 10-11: 34-64, 562-586, 861-888. Trade-language footnote pp. 48-49 (fn. 2).
sources.note: The ONLY primary attestation: five sentences of the 'Mittelsprache' (trade language) in fn. 2, p. 49, given beside Zweispitzberg-Nakanai and Open-Bay (Meramera) equivalents. Some trade-language words carry acute accent marks (Taugu, evou mi tabáriaú a pásu, a tubeni, iau mi tabar evou a buei; Amutóu me mugamuga amitéu; Iau susúgi evou la tumáli karigu; Taugu a boroi me luluéli mi tóku mi lali asava?; Evóu gologólo iau asáva?) but Hees states no rule for the trade language. The accent statements on p. 49 ('Der Akzent ist regelmäßig auf der vorletzten Silbe', Open Bay dialect = Meramera) and p.…

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia (Pacific Linguistics C-98). Canberra: ANU. pp. 258-259, 301-314 (Minigir and Tolai).

sources.access_detail: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage PL6201.R67 1988 (also: archive.org controlled lending)
sources.note: Comparative-historical monograph. Dutton & Ross identify the trade language as basically Minigir; Ross 1988 holds the only published Minigir data (field notes) and would be the place to look for a Minigir accent statement that could stand in for the trade language. Open on the PL/ANU repository but not fetched sources here because it describes Minigir (mini1251), not tola1236.

sources.citation: Rascher, Matthäus. 1897/1904 mission reports on the Massava (Massokonapuka)/Minigir people and the 1897 trip to the Nakanai coast (cited by Hees 1915-16: 48 fn. 2 as 'P. Rascher... in seinem Berichte').
